title: 6x Performance regression from dask 2024.8.0 onwards
body:
**Describe the issue**:
I am seeing a huge performance regression for certain operations using `dask>=2024.8.0`.  The below example runs over 6 times faster in 2024.7.1 than in 2024.8.0. The only difference between the two environments are the dask and distributed version.
See the timeit output:
`2024.7.1: 151 ms ± 19.3 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)`
`2024.8.0: 1.05 s ± 39.9 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)`

The example is relative complex and is using an [xclim](https://github.com/Ouranosinc/xclim) function that [generates hourly temperatures from daily min and max temperatures](https://github.com/Ouranosinc/xclim/blob/main/xclim/indices/helpers.py#L730). 

I didn't manage to narrow it down further but suspect it has something to do with the hourly resampling.

**Minimal Complete Verifiable Example**:

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from xclim.indices.helpers import make_hourly_temperature

times = pd.date_range("2000-01-01", "2010-12-31", name="time")
annual_cycle = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (times.dayofyear.values / 365.25 - 0.28))

base = 10 + 15 * annual_cycle.reshape(-1, 1)
tmin_values = base + 3 * np.random.randn(annual_cycle.size, 3)
tmax_values = base + 10 + 3 * np.random.randn(annual_cycle.size, 3)

ds = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "tasmin": (("time", "location"), tmin_values),
        "tasmax": (("time", "location"), tmax_values),
    },
    {"time": times, "location": ["IA", "IN", "IL"]},
)
ds = ds.assign_coords(lat=("location", [43.2, 40.1, 41.7]))
ds = ds.assign_coords(lat=ds.lat.assign_attrs(units="degrees_north"))
ds["tasmin"] = ds.tasmin.assign_attrs(units="degC")
ds["tasmax"] = ds.tasmax.assign_attrs(units="degC")
ds = ds.chunk(time=360, location=1)
```

```python
%%timeit

make_hourly_temperature(ds.tasmin, ds.tasmax).compute()
```

**Environment**:

- Dask version:2024.7.1/2024.8.0
- Python version: 3.11.6
- Operating System: MacOS
- Install method (conda, pip, source): PDM (pip)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi,

Is it intentional that you are using xarray backed by numpy until the Chunk command?


We made a change that keeps chunk sizes consistent internally for an operation that you are using, so we are preserving 360, 1 as chunk sizes. This is generally tiny, you should choose larger chunks and performance will get back to normal

Alright @participant1, I increased DataArray and  chunksize to 3650, 100 or 2.78 MiB and computation time is still ~2x slower in 2024.8 then 2024.7.

```python
times = pd.date_range("2000-01-01", "2050-12-31", name="time")
annual_cycle = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (times.dayofyear.values / 365.25 - 0.28))
locations = np.arange(1000)
base = 10 + 15 * annual_cycle.reshape(-1, 1)
tmin_values = base + 3 * np.random.randn(annual_cycle.size, locations.size)
tmax_values = base + 10 + 3 * np.random.randn(annual_cycle.size, locations.size)

ds = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "tasmin": (("time", "location"), tmin_values),
        "tasmax": (("time", "location"), tmax_values),
    },
    {"time": times, "location": locations},
)
ds = ds.assign_coords(lat=("location", [43.2]*locations.size))
ds = ds.assign_coords(lat=ds.lat.assign_attrs(units="degrees_north"))
ds["tasmin"] = ds.tasmin.assign_attrs(units="degC")
ds["tasmax"] = ds.tasmax.assign_attrs(units="degC")
ds = ds.chunk(time=10*365, location=100)
```

Xarray mentions chunks of a minimal chunksize of a 1M (1000x1000) so that's what I have been aiming so far.
In fact, if I change the chunks to something like 10*365 and 1000, I am getting a warning
```python
PerformanceWarning: Slicing is producing a large chunk. To accept the large
chunk and silence this warning, set the option
    >>> with dask.config.set(**{'array.slicing.split_large_chunks': False}):
    ...     array[indexer]
 ```
in 2024.7.1.


I am also quite surprised that, so much chunk optimisation is necessary to get good results on a minimal example? Would it make sense to raise a warning for small chunks. Since to me it came as quite a (hard to trace) surprise when my tests started taking much longer after I updated my environments.

comments.body:
I assume its this change that leads to the regression for chunks that are "too small" ?
https://<redacted-host>/en/stable/changelog.html#improve-scheduling-efficiency-for-xarray-groupby-reduce-patterns

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The change is this one: https://<redacted-host>/en/stable/changelog.html#improve-efficiency-and-performance-of-slicing-with-positional-indexers

previously, your example created large chunks with small inputs, which is pretty bad since it's not something you can predict. Now, you get input chunk size = output chunk size. Small input chunks will lead to small output chunks, hurting performance. 

The default chunk size behind auto is 128MiB, if you use that you should be good,

The warning is now gone since the algorithm behaves better naturally, so no warning needed anymore
